changes.title: Server code that checks "Work Orders — Create & Edit" directly changed
changes.risk_reason: A handler/voter reads this permission directly; its enforcement moved.

plain.headline: Where the app checks “Work Orders — Create & Edit” moved
plain.what: The app now checks this permission in different places behind the scenes. Usually nothing changes for users.
plain.why: A check that moved can stop working without anyone noticing on screen.
check: Log in as someone whose role has “Work Orders — Create & Edit” and try it: it should work.
Log in as someone whose role does not have it and try it: it should be blocked, and the button or page should not be shown.

qa_scenarios: API authorisation: call the affected endpoint(s) as a role WITH and a role WITHOUT "Work Orders — Create & Edit" — expect 2xx and 403.
Front end: the matching screen action is shown only to roles the API allows (front end blocks + back end allows = pass; the reverse is a defect).
Cross-role: try the same call as each system role whose defaults include or exclude the permission.

changes.title: New API endpoint guarded by a permission: GET /api/service-advisors
changes.risk_reason: New capability; confirm the guard matches the permission the PRD/story names.

plain.headline: New protected action: Viewing service advisors
plain.what: There is a new action in the app (viewing service advisors). Only people with one of 17 permissions (for example “Customers — Create & Edit” or “Customers — View”) can use it.
plain.why: A new feature: make sure the right people can use it and nobody else can.
check: Log in as someone whose role has one of the permissions listed and try it: it should work.
Log in as someone whose role has none of them and try it: it should be blocked, and the button or page should not be shown.

qa_scenarios: API authorisation: call GET /api/service-advisors as a role WITH and a role WITHOUT "Customers — Create & Edit" — expect 2xx and 403.
Front end: the matching screen action is shown only to roles the API allows (front end blocks + back end allows = pass; the reverse is a defect).
Cross-role: try the same call as each system role whose defaults include or exclude the permission.
